name: trivial_majority
notes: Trivial classifier: always predicts the majority class of the training set (PNEUMONIA). The majority class is a model parameter and is therefore estimated on train only, never on the set being evaluated. Under balanced accuracy it scores exactly 0.5 on any split by construction, so it is a floor rather than a meaningful target.

name: logreg_metadata
notes: Logistic regression on acquisition metadata only - width, height and aspect ratio - with no class weighting. Standardisation is fitted inside a Pipeline on the training split alone, so no statistics leak from validation or test. Without class weights the model minimises overall error and drifts towards the 72.7% majority class: it misclassifies 62 of the 268 validation NORMAL images, which is exactly what balanced accuracy penalises. Kept in the log as the control condition for run 003.

name: logreg_metadata_balanced
notes: Same model with class_weight=balanced, which weights each sample inversely to its class frequency and therefore aligns the training objective with the evaluation metric. Hypothesis confirmed: validation balanced accuracy rises from 0.7905 to 0.8602 against run 002. This is the reference figure of the project - roughly 0.86 of the task is solvable from acquisition metadata alone, without opening a single image, which measures how far the dataset is contaminated by provenance rather than driven by anatomy. Note also that a CNN never sees these numbers: after resizing they survive only indirectly, as resampling sharpness and geometric distortion, so this figure bounds the contamination of the dataset, not the behaviour of any given model.
